fia_question: Does a steel-equivalent rotor ring survive centrifugal load at 19,500 rpm as a SCREENING stress check?

geometry_provenance.statement: Kit-sized CalculiX ring sector from twin rotor OD/ID/active length; not the generic calculix_smoke_selftest cantilever.

magnet_pocket_burst_fea.reason: This case is a solid-ring centrifugal screen only.

margins.note: SCREENING only against assumed isotropic steel yield (355 MPa). Not laminate stack, not magnet-pocket burst, not sleeve retention, not fatigue. Never claim release FoS.

material_assumptions.label: Assumed isotropic steel screening properties — not supplier laminate stack, magnet, or retention-sleeve material cards.
material_assumptions.name: FiaFrontKitScreeningSteel

model_assumptions: Coarse C3D8 quarter-ring solid from rotor ID to OD.
Axial length = 25% of twin active/stack length.
Centrifugal *DLOAD CENTRIF at max_rotor_speed_rpm about the kit axis.
Symmetry on θ=0 (UY) and θ=90° (UX); UZ fixed on z=0 face.
No magnet pockets, bridges, sleeves, interference, or laminate anisotropy.
No case / mount / joint / torque-reaction load cases.

release_fos.statement: Screening FoS vs assumed steel yield is informational. Release factor of safety requires signed material cards, retention detail, and correlated FEA — not closed here.

release_statement: Concept evidence only. No FIA homologation, team interface closure, race evidence or permission to ship. Never claim PASS or closed release FoS from this screening case.
